meta.note: Borders are approximate. Roman provinces and client kingdoms changed often in this period, and the lines drawn here are a simplified guide. Most routes are reconstructed from the places the Gospels and Acts name.

first_passover.name: First Passover, and home through Samaria

philip.name: Philip to Samaria and the Gaza road

peter.name: Peter at Lydda, Joppa and Caesarea

snapshots.title: The birth of Jesus
snapshots.summary: Herod the Great rules a kingdom covering most of the land of Israel as a client king of Rome. Joseph and Mary travel from Nazareth to Bethlehem for the census. After the wise men's visit they flee to Egypt, then return to Nazareth after Herod's death.
snapshots.note: The Gospels don't give the route to Bethlehem; many pilgrims went down the Jordan valley to avoid Samaria. The return is drawn by the coast road.

snapshots.title: Baptism and the first disciples
snapshots.summary: Herod's kingdom is now divided. Judea is ruled by the Roman prefect Pontius Pilate, Galilee and Perea by Herod Antipas, and the lands north-east of the lake by Philip. Jesus comes from Nazareth to be baptised by John at Bethany beyond the Jordan, is tempted in the wilderness, and returns to Galilee, where he turns water into wine at Cana.
snapshots.note: Bethany beyond the Jordan is traditionally placed at al-Maghtas, near Jericho; some place it further north.

snapshots.title: The first Passover and Samaria
snapshots.summary: Jesus goes up to Jerusalem for Passover, clears the temple and talks with Nicodemus. Returning to Galilee, he passes through Samaria and meets the woman at Jacob's well near Sychar.

snapshots.title: The ministry in Galilee
snapshots.summary: Jesus makes Capernaum his base and goes throughout Galilee, teaching in the synagogues and healing. Crowds come from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea and beyond the Jordan. He crosses the lake to the Gentile eastern shore, and raises a widow's son at Nain.
snapshots.note: The places around the lake are mostly well known. The order of many Galilean events differs between the Gospels.

snapshots.title: Tyre, Sidon and Caesarea Philippi
snapshots.summary: Jesus withdraws north into Gentile territory around Tyre and Sidon, returns through the Decapolis, and then goes to the villages of Caesarea Philippi, where Peter confesses him as the Christ. Six days later he is transfigured on a high mountain.

snapshots.title: The last journey to Jerusalem
snapshots.summary: Jesus sets his face to go to Jerusalem. He goes through Perea beyond the Jordan, raises Lazarus at Bethany, passes through Jericho and enters Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives. After the resurrection he walks with two disciples on the road to Emmaus.

snapshots.title: Judea, Samaria and Damascus
snapshots.summary: Scattered by persecution, believers preach the word as they go. Philip takes the gospel to Samaria and to an Ethiopian on the Gaza road; Saul meets the risen Jesus near Damascus, goes into Arabia and is later sent home to Tarsus; Peter goes to Lydda, Joppa and the house of Cornelius at Caesarea.

snapshots.title: Paul's first journey
snapshots.summary: Sent out by the church at Antioch, Paul and Barnabas sail to Cyprus, then cross to the south coast of Asia Minor and travel inland into the province of Galatia, founding churches in Pisidian Antioch, Iconium, Lystra and Derbe, before returning the same way.

snapshots.title: Paul's second journey
snapshots.summary: Paul and Silas revisit the Galatian churches and are led by the Spirit to Troas, where Paul's vision calls them to Macedonia. The gospel reaches Europe: Philippi, Thessalonica, Berea, Athens and Corinth, where Paul stays eighteen months. He returns by Ephesus and Caesarea.

snapshots.title: Paul's third journey
snapshots.summary: Paul travels overland through Galatia to Ephesus, where he stays nearly three years. He then visits Macedonia and Greece, gathering the collection for Jerusalem, and sails back along the coast of Asia, saying farewell at Miletus, to Tyre, Caesarea and Jerusalem.
snapshots.note: From about AD 53 the lands north-east of the Sea of Galilee were given to King Agrippa II.

snapshots.title: The voyage to Rome
snapshots.summary: After two years in prison at Caesarea, Paul is sent to Rome under guard. The ship sails north of Cyprus to Myra, changes to a grain ship, and creeps along the south of Crete before a storm drives it west for two weeks to shipwreck on Malta. In spring Paul sails on by Syracuse to Puteoli and walks the Appian Way to Rome.
snapshots.note: The traditional site of the shipwreck is St Paul's Bay on Malta; the storm's route across the open sea is approximate.

snapshots.title: Paul's last years
snapshots.summary: Acts ends with Paul under house arrest in Rome. His letters to Timothy and Titus suggest that he was released and travelled again to Crete, Ephesus, Troas, Macedonia and Nicopolis, before a second imprisonment in Rome and his death under Nero.
snapshots.note: This route is reconstructed from the letters and is uncertain; the order of the places is not known. Some scholars think Paul was never released.
